 Senior Night Matchup with American Ahead for Navy Women's Soccer
 Mids to honor the careers of their seven seniors at 6:45 PM prior to the contest
 Story Links
 Live Video 
 Live Stats 
 Game Notes 
 ANNAPOLIS, Md. - Senior Night festivities celebrating the Navy Women's Soccer Class of 2027 highlights this weekend's slate of action at the Glenn Warner Soccer Facility. Prior to Friday night's matchup with American University, Navy will honor the seven members of its graduating class with a brief ceremony beginning at 6:45 p.m. After that presentation the focus of the Mids (11-4-2, 4-1-1 PL) will squarely flip back to the pitch as they look to continue strengthening their position near the top of the Patriot League standings with a 7 p.m. showdown versus the Eagles (0-10-4, 0-4-2 PL). A glance at the conference table shows Navy in second place with 13 points, just a game behind Army (16) and two points ahead of Loyola and Bucknell, who each have secured 11 points through six league contests. 
The seven seniors to be honored include: Ali Barrow , Chiara Cosenza , Lucy Gaines , Hannah Mulholland , Cadence Tordai , Madison Whitworth and  ClaraJane Williams .
The Navy-American contest will have live stats provided online, as well as an accompanying ESPN+ broadcast. ESPN+ is a subscription-based streaming service that requires patrons to sign-up for monthly or yearly plans prior to tuning into the contest. 
 Navy vs. American 
Friday will be the 35th meeting between the two nearby schools in a series that began on Sept. 7, 1994 ... Navy leads the series 21-9-4 and has outscored American, 63-31 all-time ... The Mids are 10-4-2 when matching up with the Eagles in Annapolis, though are even over the last three contests at Glenn Warner (1-1-1) ... Navy and American have gone through large momentum swings throughout this series as the Mids won the first four meetings from 1994-1998 before stringing together a recent run of 15 games with just a single loss (13-1-1) from 2011-2023, including two postseason victories during that span ... During that 13-year run of recent play for Navy, the Mids outscored the Eagles, 31-7.
     Last Five Matchups 
    In the last five meetings dating back to 2021, Navy is 3-2 and has outscored American, 6-2 ... All five contests have involved clean sheets for the victor
    Oct. 15, 2025 (A): Navy 3 - American 0
    Oct. 16, 2024 (H): American 1 - Navy 0
    Oct. 11, 2023 (A): American 1 - Navy 0
    Oct. 12, 2022 (H): Navy 1 - American 0
    Oct. 13, 2021 (A): Navy 2 - American 0
 Most Recent Navy-American Matchup: Oct. 15, 2025 in Washington, D.C. 
After a recent string of tight heart-breaking results, the Navy women's soccer team left little to chance on Wednesday as the Mids went on the road to American University and dominated the Eagles to the tune of a 3-0 victory. The Mids (9-5-2, 2-2-2 PL) took the lead over the Eagles (2-9-3, 2-4-0 PL) on a Chiara Cosenza goal in the seventh minute and never looked back with two additional scores in the second half.
Cosenza paced Navy's offense with a pair of goals on Wednesday afternoon at Reeves Field as she added her second score in the 60th minute. Marlee Heaven continued to play a leading role in the Mids' attack with a goal in the 52nd minute and an assist. Sophomore goalkeeper Natasha Stramrood backstopped the Navy's defense with seven saves over the 90-minute shutout performance.
Looking to impose their style of play, the Mids came out of the gates on a mission on Wednesday. After Stramrood turned aside a pair of American shots over the opening three minutes, Cosenza focused on getting Navy on the scoreboard with a shot on goal in the third minute and a second attempt that just missed off target in the sixth minute. The junior made her third attempt of the early goings count when she ran up on a deflected Heaven shot and struck home the loose ball to give the Mids at 1-0 at 6:22.
Stramrood was the story of the next 38-plus minutes of the half as she continued to withstand every scoring opportunity by the Eagles with three additional saves. Central defender Jordan Townsend also played a key role in this first half shutout as the team captain raced back on a breakaway by American's Jenna Etienne-Valtrin in the 32nd minute and slide-tackled the ball away from danger before the Eagle forward could unleash a shot.
Holding just a one-goal lead coming out of the locker room, the visiting Mids almost immediately pounced on the opportunity to double their lead as just over six minutes into play, Hannah Mulholland dribbled in from the right wing, slotted a square pass to Lizzie Emerson , who turned to her left and laid the ball to a wide open Heaven at the top of the 18-yard box. With time and space to play with Heaven surveyed her options and flicked a looping shot over the American goalkeeper into the far corner of the goal at 51:19.
Less than eight minutes later at 59:05, the Mids' crisp passing was showcased again when Jessica Black navigated her way through the Eagles' defense and played a square ball to Katia Katsari-Hoefer , who dummied a shot and deflected the ball on a bit further into the box where the hard-charging Cosenza one-timed a shot low and through the hands of American's goalkeeper for her second goal of the game.
In control of the game, 3-0 with 30 minutes to go, Navy kept its foot on the proverbial gas pedal in all facets of the action with its offense continuing to pepper Addison Roemer, American's goalkeeper with two additional shots on goal, while Stramrood and the Mids' defense held the Eagles to just two easily denied looks at goal to clinch the 3-0 shutout victory.
For the game, Navy out-shot American, 19-11 with a 9-7 edge in shots on goal. The host Eagles had a 5-2 advantage in corner kicks. After making five saves in first half, Stramrood completed her clean sheet outing with seven stops.

 Last Time Out: Friday, Oct. 16 vs. Bucknell in Annapolis  
A promising matchup between Navy and Bucknell, two teams separated by just one point in the Patriot League standings, had all types of twists and turns as part of a one-goal contest on Friday night. At the end of 90 minutes of action, the Mids (11-4-2, 4-1-1 PL) came out on top of the Bison (6-6-3, 3-1-2 PL) by a score of 1-0 on the strength of a Chiara Cosenza penalty kick in the 83rd minute.
The initial kickoff at the Glenn Warner Soccer Facility was moved up an hour in advance of potential inclement weather as both squads hoped to complete play before a substantial band of rain and high winds was set to enter the Annapolis region. Helpful for the first half, which was played in warm, summer-like conditions, that inclement weather eventually reared its ugly head with torrential downpours and wind gusts whipping over 30 miles per hour and played a significant role in the second half.
Junior goalkeeper Natasha Stramrood was strong in goal as she posted her second consecutive shutout with five saves.
While the field was fast and dry in the first half, the action bounced from end to end up and down the pitch as both teams were active out of the gate with Navy registering three shots over the opening 10:25 and Bucknell tallying back-to-back attempts in the 12th minute.
After that initial feeling out period, more defensive-minded and physical play took control of the middle portion of the first half with only one total shot taken over the next 20 minutes. In the 33rd minute, Stramrood's number was called as Ingrid Murphy took aim for the back of the net following a corner kick opportunity. A little over three minutes later, Stramrood was up to the task again with another save, her third of the half.
Scoreless coming out of the locker rooms after the halftime intermission, the evenly-matched play that marked the first half went out the window as Mother Nature took control within minutes of the teams re-taking the field. After the squads exchanged shots in the 49th and 50th minutes, the Bison were held to just two more shots for the final 40 minutes of play as they were dealing with a smothering defensive effort by the Mids and a substantial wind blowing into their attack. Likewise, Navy used this to its advantage with booming punts and a willingness to take shots from slightly further out with the wind behind them and a slick goal box.
 Ande Swan notched the Mids' second shot on goal of the half with a deep blast from outside the 18 in the 55th minute before Katia Katsari-Hoefer recorded the host's most dangerous look as her shot zipped past Sarah McFarland, but unfortunately square into the cross bar in the 77th minute. 70 seconds later, Stella Jones tallied her second shot on goal of the game as her seemingly innocent cross, kept curling and forced McFarland to leap up and make a save.
With the game still scoreless and less than 10 minutes remaining, Helen Bonner took aim with a shot on a goal in the 82nd minute before Dani Howard switched the field and had a rebuttal for Bucknell 33 seconds later.
As the rain slowed and wind settled the scoreboard finally saw action at 82:12 when Cosenza was fouled in the box and was awarded a penalty kick. The senior sharpshooter had no qualms about taking the PK and calmly deposited it into the corner of the goal to give Navy the eventual game-winning score as neither team recorded a shot over the remaining 7:48 of play.
For the game, Navy out-shot Bucknell, 18-8 with a 7-5 edge in shots on goal. The Mids also held a slight advantage in corner kicks, 6-4.
Stramrood completed her fourth solo shutout of the season and the team's eighth overall with five saves. She's currently on a run of 244:15 straight minutes of scoreless action in goal.
 Parking / Shuttle 
Fans are reminded that the general public does not have access to drive their vehicles on to the U.S. Naval Academy. Fans may park at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium for a fee and take a shuttle that will run every 10 minutes starting one hour before the game and will continue running until one hour after the game is completed. Enter Gate 5 off Taylor Ave. to park at the stadium. Fans 18 and over need a government-issued photo ID. 
**Starting May 7, 2025, in accordance with The Real ID Act of 2005, visitors entering through the Pedestrian Gate 1 Visitor Control Center or accessing the USNA through the fan shuttle bus for a game should be prepared to present a REAL ID-compliant driver's license, U.S. Passport, enhanced state-issued ID, or another acceptable form of identification, to access federal facilities.  Foreign passports are NOT permitted for general access.
